newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Costello to travel to U.S..
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Costello to travel to U.S..

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello will travel to the United States to attend a series of World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF) meetings from September 27 to October 3, his office said on Tuesday.

Costello will attend an IMF interim committee meeting on September 29, an IMF and World Bank development committee meeting on September 30, and IMF and World Bank annual meetings on October 1, his office said in a statement.
"While in Washington the Treasurer will also have a number of bilateral meetings," the statement said.
Costello will also travel to New York on October 2 for a series of meetings and address an Asia Society lunch on October 3, his office said.
Australia's conservative Liberal-National government, which ousted the Labor Party in a landslide election win on March 2, has set closer ties with Washington as a foreign policy priority.
Acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer said last week that U.S. President Bill Clinton's visit to Australia in November affirmed this close relationship.
The United States plays a crucial economic and strategic role in the Asia-Pacific, Fischer said.

The United States is Australia's second-largest trading partner, with two-way trade worth A$20.7 billion in the year to June 30, 1995, according to Trade Department figures. Australia's trade deficit with the U.S. was A$11.4 billion.
